record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is infinite and separable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is an infinite separable topological group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological group is a group $G$ equipped with a topology making the group operations (multiplication and inversion) continuous. A topological space is called separable if it contains a countable dense subset. A topological group $G$ is totally disconnected if the connected component of the identity (equivalently, of every point) is trivial. A quotient group of a topological group $G$ is a group of the form $G/N$ where $N$ is a closed normal subgroup of $G$, endowed with the quotient topology.

Question: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group $G$ admit a closed normal subgroup $N$ such that the quotient topological group $G/N$ is both infinite and separable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. A 2017 work (published in the Israel Journal of Mathematics, 2019) shows that not every non-totally disconnected topological group has a separable quotient that is (i) non-trivial, (ii) infinite, (iii) metrizable, or (iv) infinite metrizable; all four versions, including the "infinite" version posed here, are resolved negatively. Positive answers are established for special classes such as compact groups, locally compact abelian groups, σ-compact locally compact groups, abelian pro-Lie groups, σ-compact pro-Lie groups, and pseudocompact groups.

status_evidence.title: The Separable Quotient Problem for Topological Groups
status_evidence.snippet: All four questions are answered here in the negative... Positive answers ... are proved for groups G which belong to ... compact groups; locally compact abelian groups; ... pseudocompact groups.
status_evidence.claim: The infinite separable quotient question for non-totally disconnected topological groups is answered in the negative in general, with positive results for several important classes.

status_evidence.title: The separable quotient problem for topological groups (Israel J. Math.)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version in Israel Journal of Mathematics resolving the separable quotient problem for topological groups.
status_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed publication confirms the negative resolution of the general question.
